patient.name: Robert Kimura
patient.chief_complaint: Bilateral foot tingling and numbness for 2 years in a patient with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma
patient.hpi: Robert Kimura is a 53-year-old retired financial analyst who was diagnosed with IgG kappa multiple myeloma 6 months ago and has been receiving bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (VRd) chemotherapy. He now presents to neurology for evaluation of bilateral foot tingling and numbness that began 6 weeks after his first bortezomib cycle and has progressively worsened over 4 cycles. The symptoms began in the bilateral great toes and have spread to involve all toes and the forefoot on both sides. He describes the sensation as 'electric shocks with pins and needles' predominantly, with a burning component at night. He also notes bilateral fingertip tingling that began 2 weeks ago. He does not have significant weakness, though he notices mild clumsiness with buttons. He denies ataxia or falls. His oncologist has been monitoring him and has already dose-reduced bortezomib from 1.3 mg/m² to 1.0 mg/m² after cycle 3 due to these symptoms. He has no prior history of neuropathy, no diabetes, no alcohol use. He was an active runner prior to his myeloma diagnosis and is very motivated to return to running if possible.

output.query: bortezomib peripheral neuropathy management dose modification IMWG

results.citation: Moreau P et al. (2011) Subcutaneous versus intravenous bortezomib for myeloma. Lancet Oncol 12:431-440.
results.summary: Subcutaneous bortezomib (SC) reduces grade ≥3 PN from 16% (IV) to 6% with equivalent efficacy. SC dosing is now standard of care. Grade 1: 1.3 mg/m² dose maintained. Grade 2: dose reduce to 1.0 mg/m². Grade 3: hold bortezomib, resume at 0.7 mg/m² when ≤grade 1. Grade 4: discontinue permanently.

results.citation: Richardson PG et al. (2012) Prevention and management of treatment-emergent peripheral neuropathy in multiple myeloma. J Clin Oncol 30:3573-3580.
results.summary: Weekly bortezomib administration (rather than twice-weekly) reduces neuropathy incidence. SC route preferred. Symptoms often partially reversible after discontinuation. Carfilzomib or ixazomib are alternatives with lower neurotoxicity for patients with significant BiPN.

output.summary: Randomized trial data demonstrate that subcutaneous bortezomib administration significantly reduces the incidence of severe peripheral neuropathy compared to intravenous administration with equivalent anti-myeloma efficacy. Published dose-modification guidelines stratify bortezomib neuropathy by NCI CTCAE grade. Weekly bortezomib dosing is associated with lower neuropathy incidence compared to twice-weekly. Carfilzomib and ixazomib have lower peripheral neurotoxicity profiles and are used in patients with significant bortezomib-induced neuropathy. Symptoms of bortezomib-induced peripheral neuropathy often partially or fully reverse after drug discontinuation or dose reduction.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Bortezomib-induced peripheral neuropathy (BiPN), NCI CTCAE grade 2, in multiple myeloma
critical_actions: Grade the neuropathy severity using NCI CTCAE scale — drives dose modification decisions
Confirm SC bortezomib (not IV) — reduces neuropathy risk by 60%
MRI spine to exclude cord compression — myeloma patients with new neurological symptoms always need this
Serial NCS monitoring — if grade 3, hold bortezomib; if grade 4, discontinue permanently
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue bortezomib at full dose in grade 2 neuropathy without dose reduction — dose modification is standard protocol
Do not switch to IV bortezomib — SC route has significantly less neurotoxicity
Do not prescribe tricyclic antidepressants first-line — duloxetine is preferred (FDA-approved for chemotherapy-induced neuropathy)

key_reasoning_points: STRAIGHTFORWARD REAL-SEEDED: Classic presentation of bortezomib-induced peripheral neuropathy in multiple myeloma — temporal correlation, sensory predominance, length-dependent pattern
KEY MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLE: Dose modification based on CTCAE grade is mandatory — grade 2 = reduce to 1.0 mg/m², grade 3 = hold, grade 4 = discontinue
SC ROUTE: Subcutaneous bortezomib produces equivalent anti-myeloma efficacy with 60% reduction in severe neuropathy — SC is now standard of care
WEEKLY vs TWICE-WEEKLY: Weekly dosing also reduces neurotoxicity — useful if grade 2 neuropathy persists despite SC route
